18.description: The committee recommends increasing the North Yards land development budget by $44,000 and changing its $3.75 million funding from property sales to internal borrowing.

chips.text: Staff could not confirm original relocation plans for surplus city properties.

20.description: Committee recommends City Council approve 2026 budgets for five Business Improvement Districts, which determine levies on commercial properties in their areas.

chips.text: Councillor questioned increased board expenses for two BIDs; director explained restoration.
Administration only receives BID budgets, does not review or question amounts.

21.description: The committee recommends adding a $1.5 million contingency to the 2026 property tax levy for commercial and industrial properties to cover appeal losses.

22.description: The committee recommends a five-year property tax exemption for the 602 (Lynx) Wing Saskatoon R.C.A.F. Association at 2407 Avenue C North.

chips.text: Mayor Block questioned if the city reviews the actual usage of tax-exempt properties.

24.description: The committee recommends a land exchange between Prairieland Park, the Western Development Museum, and the City, creating two new city development parcels on Lorne Avenue.

chips.text: Councillor Diploc wants to know if partners will share subdivision costs.
Prairieland Park and Western Development Museum will receive reconfigured, larger lease areas.
Exact cost-sharing for subdivision among parties is still to be negotiated.
Administration will communicate cost-sharing details when development parcels are sold.

25.description: Saskatoon Land is authorized to sell two multi-unit parcels in Aspen Ridge for $1.2 million and $1 million per acre via open market.

chips.text: Purchasers are targeting purpose-built rental unit projects.

27.description: The committee recommends City Council transfer a $195,616 civic operations deficit from the Fiscal Stabilization Reserve and move $4 million from the Water and Wastewater Stabilization Reserve to fund infrastructure.

chips.text: Councillor Dubois noted asset management success in reducing water main breaks.
Future water rates may be reduced by infrastructure reserve transfers.
Administration was unsure if Nutrient still contributes money for Playland naming rights.
Administration will provide committee with Nutrient Playland naming rights terms.

29.description: The committee recommends Saskatoon purchase 106 Tubby Crescent for $6.3 million to establish a new Fire Department fleet maintenance facility, transferring $7.4 million to 2026 for the project.

chips.text: Other civic divisions will gain storage for off-season equipment and materials.

28.description: Saskatoon will not pursue a property tax subclass for vacant buildings, as administrative costs outweigh benefits and current enforcement efforts are effective.

chips.text: Moose Jaw eliminated its vacant commercial property tax subclass due to ineffectiveness.
Provincial tax rate limits may restrict how much the city could charge with a subclass.

23.description: The committee recommends City Council appoint Mayor Block, or Councillors Dubois or Kelleher, as proxy for the City at the 2026 AGMs of the Centennial Auditorium boards.

chips.text: Saskatoon Centennial Auditorium Convention Centre Corporation and Foundation.

26.description: Saskatoon City Council appointed Mayor Block, or Councillors Davies or Parker, as its proxy to vote at the Saskatchewan Place Association Inc. Annual General Meeting on April 16, 2026.
